newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Foreign shares up in Pakistan State Oil.
newsitem.headline: Foreign shares up in Pakistan State Oil.

text.p: Foreign investment in state-run Pakistan State Oil (PSO) rose to 23 percent by June 30 from 18.84 percent one year previously, a company spokesman said on Monday.
PSO's 10-rupee share rose 10 rupees, or 2.63 percent, to 390 on Monday on buying by foreign fund managers, dealers said.
"The blue chip is in heavy demand amid overseas investors," dealer Azhar Batla of Taurus Securities said.
Some 17,500 shares changed hands on Monday, he said.

The company has already paid 30 percent interim cash dividend for fiscal 1996/97 (July-June). Its pre-tax profit for the first half of fiscal 1996/97 rose 58 percent to 869 million ($21.39 million) rupees from 548 million in the year-ago period.
The company paid 60 percent dividend and 30 percent in bonus shares for the year ended June 30, 1997 compared to 50 percent dividend and 30 percent bonus stocks a year ago.
